documents: Menges et al. 2022, JGR Biogeosciences 127, e2022JG007126 (published paper, PDF, 18 pages)

entry.evidence: Here, we employ FT-ICR-MS for the first time to trace the lipid component of particulate organic matter through a natural landscape.

steps.action: Frame the problem: source apportionment and transformation of particulate organic matter from source to sink are hard to resolve with isotopes or a few biomarkers.
steps.quote: it is thus essential to trace the sourcing and transport as well as transformation and remineralization

steps.action: Take from the literature the capability of ESI-FT-ICR-MS to assign thousands of molecular formulas in complex organic mixtures without chromatography.
steps.quote: Fourier Transform Ion Cyclotron Resonance Mass Spectrometry (FT-ICR-MS) has emerged as a powerful tool

steps.action: Propose applying FT-ICR-MS to solvent-extractable lipids of particulate organic matter across a landscape, both to screen for source markers and to track transformations.
steps.quote: Here, we employ FT-ICR-MS for the first time to trace the lipid component of particulate organic matter through a natural landscape

steps.action: Use the authors' earlier bulk-isotope (Bayesian mixing) result that topsoil, paleosol and petrogenic carbon are all mobilized by the Kali Gandaki River.
steps.quote: have been shown to get mobilized by the Kali Gandaki River based on bulk isotope analyses

steps.action: Select 53 source and river sediment samples from the sample set collected for the earlier study during the 2015 and 2016 monsoons.
steps.quote: we used 53 samples from a larger sample set collected in the upper KG catchment during consecutive monsoon seasons in 2015 and 2016

steps.action: Soxhlet-extract lipids, measure them by negative-mode ESI on a 12 T FT-ICR-MS, assign formulas above the method detection limit, drop four low-abundance spectra, and build relative-abundance and presence-absence data sets.
steps.quote: Mass spectrometric analyses were performed on a 12 T FT-ICR mass spectrometer

steps.action: Adopt the thermodynamic expectation (LaRowe & Van Cappellen 2011) that high-NOSC compounds are preferentially oxidized, alongside the DBE and elemental-ratio metrics.
steps.quote: compounds with high NOSC values are generally interpreted to have low stability

steps.action: Describe molecular metrics by sample type (litter-topsoil-paleosol trend, diverse bedrock, intermediate river samples) and ordinate all samples by NMDS, finding distinct clusters except tributaries.
steps.quote: In the corresponding ordination space, all sample types formed distinct clusters, except the tributary samples.

steps.action: Repeat the NMDS with Jaccard (presence-absence) and Bray-Curtis (relative abundance) dissimilarities and compare the groupings.
steps.quote: Both NMDS analyses revealed generally similar groupings of the organic

steps.action: Propose that tributary samples trending away from all sampled sources reflect unsampled sources such as aquatic production.
steps.quote: the catchment may contain additional organic matter sources that have not been sampled in this study

steps.action: Apply indicator species analysis (999 randomizations, p<0.05, indicator value >0.7) to find indicator formulas for topsoil, paleosol, bedrock and combined biospheric sources, excluding the CHN-dominated bedrock sample.
steps.quote: To test for potential groups of such indicator compounds we performed indicator species analysis (ISA)

steps.action: Run ISA on both the presence-absence and relative-abundance data and compare the composition of the indicator sets.
steps.quote: the characteristic composition of indicator MFs for each source was remarkably similar

steps.action: Count source indicator formulas in river sediments and compare with the bulk-isotope finding that all three sources reach the river.
steps.quote: indicator MFs for all three organic matter sources could be generally detected in river sediment samples

steps.action: Offer rivals for the low and variable indicator detection in the river: charge competition in ESI, petrogenic facies variability, and chemical transformation in transit.
steps.quote: These differences may be in part due to charge competition effects

steps.action: Argue that charge competition plays only a minor role, because sediment total ion abundance was below a critical level and only presence is considered.
steps.quote: this should only play a minor role

steps.action: Ask whether FT-ICR-MS detects molecular transformations along known pathways that bulk measurements miss.
steps.quote: we have tested whether it is possible to detect molecular transformations of particulate organic matter

steps.action: Take from prior studies the expectation that wax-lipid and isoprenoid patterns are preserved, with partial degradation, as litter enters soil.
steps.quote: characteristic patterns of wax lipids and isoprenoids are preserved as fresh plant material is incorporated into soil organic matter

steps.action: Compare three same-site litter-topsoil pairs: shared and specific formulas, cumulative abundance, carbon-number pattern, and DBE and NOSC distributions.
steps.quote: The cumulative relative abundance of the shared MFs was 89 ± 3% in the litter samples

steps.action: Keep efficient incorporation of litter lipids into topsoil, with small shifts to lower O/C, DBE and NOSC consistent with partial degradation.
steps.quote: is congruent with the active incorporation of plant-derived extractable lipids into the topsoil

steps.action: State the expectation that main-river sediment, fed by all sources, should have high molecular richness.
steps.quote: we expected the molecular richness (i.e., the number of different MFs for each sample type) of main river sediment to be comparably high

steps.action: Compare aggregated richness (4,031 source formulas versus 1,147 river formulas) and find that the expectation fails, with a large loss of formulas.
steps.quote: the total molecular richness of the main river sediment samples was only 1,147

steps.action: Suggest a possible aquatic origin for the 80 river-specific formulas, 41 of them CHNO.
steps.quote: 41 of those MFs were CHNO MFs hinting at a potential aquatic origin

steps.action: Characterize lost versus persistent formulas per source (Figure 7): shared topsoil and bedrock formulas skew to low DBE and NOSC; paleosol formulas show little shift.
steps.quote: MFs shared between topsoils and main river sediment samples had a much smaller range in DBEs

steps.action: Recheck the trends after restricting to formulas present in at least two samples and when comparing individual source and river samples.
steps.quote: [...] in molecular metrics were still evident when restricting the data set to MFs that occurred in at least two samples

steps.action: List rival causes of the selective loss: methodological (sampling bias, dilution, ESI signal suppression) and natural (desorption then degradation, direct microbial degradation).
steps.quote: Potential reasons for these apparent transformations can be factors inherent in our method, as well as natural processes.

steps.action: Derive the prediction that dilution or signal suppression would produce covariation between molecular metrics and relative abundance.
steps.quote: this should be visible in a covariation of molecular metrics and the relative abundance

steps.action: Reject dilution and suppression (no covariation found; river samples less diverse and less abundant), and set aside salinity-driven desorption because no such conditions exist upstream; sampling bias argued against but not excluded.
steps.quote: we do not consider dilution and/or signal suppression to be a major cause of the observed pattern

steps.action: Retain microbially mediated degradation as the plausible, tentative explanation, consistent with NOSC trends and the absence of riparian vegetation.
steps.quote: We tentatively attribute this to microbially mediated direct degradation of compounds, but cannot exclude other mechanisms.

steps.action: Conclude that FT-ICR-MS on extractable lipids characterizes and discriminates particulate organic matter sources and detects transformations.
steps.quote: This confirms the suitability of FT-ICR-MS data on extractable lipids for the characterization and differentiation of particulate organic matter types

tree.answer: Distinct molecular composition of organic matter pools; selective loss of formulas from source to river
Molecular formulas measured directly; structures and processes not observed
Characterize FT-ICR-MS for source fingerprinting and tracking transformations
For formula loss: sampling bias, dilution or signal suppression, desorption-degradation, microbial degradation
Dilution or suppression predicts covariation of metrics with abundance; none found
Found: natural catchment, monsoon samples, same-site litter-topsoil pairs
Groupings and trends robust to dissimilarity metric, data transformation and data subsets
Capability characterized; microbial degradation tentatively best explanation

end.claim: ESI-FT-ICR-MS of extractable lipids discriminates particulate organic matter sources (up to about 100 indicator formulas per source) and detects molecular transformations from litter to soil and from sources to the river.

decisive_move.sentence: Without the ESI-FT-ICR-MS measurement of source and river lipid extracts there would be no formula data sets on which the source discrimination and transformation claims rest.

gates.evidence: Samples were reused from an earlier study and screened untargeted, so no stated hypothesis directed acquisition (p. 4). The richness expectation could fail and did (p. 12). The capability claim rests on clusters that could have failed to separate (p. 7). The dilution rival met a stated test (p. 14). Nothing is reported as fixed before the data were seen.

imports.item: Indicator species analysis (Dufrêne & Legendre 1997; indicspecies package)
Molecular richness, by analogy with species richness
NMDS with Jaccard and Bray-Curtis dissimilarities
Double bond equivalents and van Krevelen diagrams
Welch ANOVA, Games-Howell, Kruskal-Wallis and Dunn tests with Bonferroni correction

novelty_claims.quote: Here, we employ FT-ICR-MS for the first time to trace the lipid component of particulate organic matter through a natural landscape.
untargeted FT-ICR-MS analysis can reveal previously unknown shifts in molecular composition along organic matter pathways in the environment

limits: No peer-review file was supplied, so only the final-paper sequence is coded. Samples were collected for an earlier study, so acquisition was not directed by this paper's questions. Source groups are small (3 litter, 3 paleosol, 6 bedrock), and the paper reports no replicate injections, procedural blanks or instrument reproducibility (inference: not shown). Formulas are not structures, as the authors note. Sub-claim statuses: efficient litter-to-topsoil incorporation is best_explanation (three pairs, no rival tested); selective loss of high-DBE and high-NOSC formulas is a regularity across sources stated without a range; microbial degradation is a tentative best_explanation, with sampling bias not excluded; the aquatic origin of river-specific CHNO formulas and unsampled tributary sources are untested hypotheses. The Figure 2 caption gives the same sample name for topsoil and paleosol, apparently a typo. No pre-registration.

disagreements.target: Lipids generally considered recalcitrant compounds (e.g., Lorenz et al., 2007)
disagreements.support: Low-abundance lipid formulas are lost between sources and the river, suggesting recalcitrance does not hold for all lipid compounds.
disagreements.quote: this may not systematically apply to compounds that are only present in low abundances

disagreements.target: Menges et al. (2020): no decomposition detected in bulk organic carbon isotope data
disagreements.support: Molecular data show a selective loss of high-DBE and high-NOSC formulas from sources to the river, which the paper frames as adding detail to the earlier bulk result.
disagreements.quote: no changes reflecting decomposition were detected using bulk organic carbon isotope data

disagreements.support: Targeted chromatographic methods cover a narrow mass range and need laborious preparation, whereas FT-ICR-MS screens thousands of formulas at once.
disagreements.quote: These factors prevent the rapid and systematic screening for new potential biomarkers

alternatives_considered.chosen: Both Jaccard (presence-absence) and Bray-Curtis (relative abundance) NMDS
alternatives_considered.reason: Jaccard weights all formulas equally; Bray-Curtis weights abundant formulas

alternatives_considered.chosen: Presence-absence indicator formulas for further investigation
alternatives_considered.reason: Given the ionization effects of ESI

alternatives_considered.chosen: Exclude bedrock sample JM26/R26 from NMDS and ISA
alternatives_considered.reason: Dissimilar to all other samples; dominated by CHN formulas

alternatives_considered.chosen: Welch ANOVA with Games-Howell, or Kruskal-Wallis with Dunn
alternatives_considered.reason: Variances unequal; normality not always met
none given for the choice; APPI noted to have a better concentration response

alternatives_considered.alternatives: Sampling bias; dilution below detection or ESI signal suppression; desorption followed by degradation
alternatives_considered.reason: No covariation of metrics with abundance; no salinity changes or fresh organic matter upstream; no riparian vegetation

alternatives_considered.chosen: Aggregated richness data sets per sample type
alternatives_considered.alternatives: Formulas in at least two samples; individual sample comparisons
